clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old female with autoimmune hepatitis/primary biliary cholangitis overlap syndrome (diagnosed 2014) presented in July 2021 for delayed follow-up of an incidentally detected 9-10mm subcapsular hypoechoic hepatic nodule in segment VI/VII found on ultrasound in October 2020. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the recommended 3-month follow-up was not performed. In July 2021, an atypical resection of the VIIth hepatic segment was performed. Histological examination of the resected specimen revealed moderately differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma (G2) with predominant solid architecture, no tumoral necrosis, and intact liver capsule. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated HepPar-1 positivity, Glypican-3 positivity, and CD34 positivity indicating sinusoidal capillarization. Pathological staging was pT2 L0 V1 R0. A resected lymph node showed no malignant cells, supporting N0 classification. The patient was classified as BCLC Stage A, indicating suitability for curative surgical treatment.
